questions.q: What makes a value 'disaggregated' (row-level) rather than 'aggregated'?
options: It's the raw value for one individual record, with no aggregate function like SUM or AVG applied to it
It's always a text field, never a number
It comes from a calculated field rather than the raw data source
It has been filtered out of the view
questions.explain: A disaggregated value is the raw, row-level value before any aggregate function (SUM, AVG, COUNT, MIN, MAX) summarizes it across multiple rows.

questions.q: Why is SUM([Sales]) * [Quantity] an invalid Tableau calculation?
options: SUM([Sales]) is aggregated but [Quantity] is disaggregated, and Tableau doesn't allow mixing the two in one expression
Multiplication isn't a supported operator in Tableau
SUM can only be used on the Quantity field, not Sales
The formula is missing an END keyword
questions.explain: Per Tableau's own documentation, for any aggregate calculation you cannot combine an aggregated value and a disaggregated value in the same expression — SUM([Sales]) is aggregated, [Quantity] alone is not.

questions.q: Which of these is a valid fix for the invalid formula SUM([Sales]) * [Quantity]?
options: SUM([Sales]) * SUM([Quantity]) — aggregating both sides
SUM([Sales]) * [Quantity] with quotes added around Quantity
Removing the multiplication operator entirely
Renaming Quantity to avoid the error
questions.explain: Aggregating both sides (or aggregating neither) resolves the mismatch — SUM([Sales]) * SUM([Quantity]) keeps both sides consistently aggregated.

questions.q: Why does Profit Ratio need to be written as SUM([Profit]) / SUM([Sales]) rather than [Profit] / SUM([Sales])?
options: [Profit] alone is disaggregated while SUM([Sales]) is aggregated — mixing them causes the same error as the SUM(Sales) * Quantity example
Division requires at least one side to be disaggregated
SUM() is only needed for the numerator, never the denominator
There's no real difference — both versions are equally valid
questions.explain: Mixing an aggregated denominator with a disaggregated numerator is exactly the same aggregate/non-aggregate mismatch covered earlier in the lesson — both sides need SUM() to be valid.

questions.q: What does the error 'Cannot mix aggregate and non-aggregate arguments with this function' tell you to look for?
options: One field in the formula that isn't aggregated when it should be (or vice versa), so the two sides of an operator don't match
A missing END keyword somewhere in the formula
A field with the wrong data type, like text being compared to a number
A NULL value silently propagating through the calculation
questions.explain: This specific error is about aggregation level mismatches — the fix is finding the field that isn't wrapped in an aggregate function (or shouldn't be) and correcting the mismatch, not a data-type or NULL issue.
